name: Central Teacher Eligibility Test
summary: The national teacher eligibility test. Paper I qualifies you to teach Classes I to V and Paper II Classes VI to VIII in KVS, NVS and other central schools. The certificate is valid for life. It is not a job by itself.

status.note: The 22nd edition was first set for 6 September 2026 and later moved to 12 and 13 December 2026 by CBSE notice. Applications closed on 10 June 2026.

posts.name: CTET certificate (Paper I and/or Paper II)
posts.responsibilities: Makes you eligible to apply for teacher posts in central government schools and CBSE schools.

age.summary: The bulletin sets no upper age limit for the test.

education.summary: Minimum qualifications as notified by NCTE. Paper I: Senior Secondary (Class 12) with a teacher-training diploma such as D.El.Ed. Paper II: a degree with B.Ed. Final-year trainees may appear. Reserved categories get up to 5% relaxation in qualifying marks.

attempts.limit: No limit; qualified candidates may retake to improve their score

eligibility.examVsPost: Passing CTET gives no job. You still need to clear a recruitment such as KVS/NVS, where CTET is one eligibility condition.
eligibility.reservation: Central reservation: SC 15%, ST 7.5%, OBC (non-creamy layer) 27%, EWS 10%, plus horizontal reservation for PwBD and ex-servicemen as per rules.

eligibilityRules.notes: Paper I needs a teacher-training diploma after Class 12; Paper II needs a degree with B.Ed.

stages.name: Paper I and/or Paper II (OMR, objective)

papers.name: Paper I (Classes I to V): Child Development and Pedagogy 30, Language I 30, Language II 30, Mathematics 30, Environmental Studies 30
Paper II (Classes VI to VIII): Child Development and Pedagogy 30, Language I 30, Language II 30, Mathematics and Science or Social Studies 60

stages.notes: All questions are multiple choice with four options.

selection.meritCalculation: Qualifying test: 60% or more is a pass (NCTE notification of 11 Feb 2011). Schools may give concessions to reserved categories.
selection.languages: English, Hindi and a list of languages for Language I and II.

sections.subject: Four sections
topics: Mathematics and science (60) or social studies (60)

salary.notes: No salary: this is an eligibility test.

progression.post: Teacher in a central school (after recruitment)
progression.timeline: After a recruitment such as KVS/NVS

career.promotionNotes: See KVS and NVS teacher recruitment.

difficulty.rationale: Qualifying test with no limit on attempts; the 60% pass mark still filters many.

ratings.rationale: Held often and valid for life; the job depends on teacher recruitments.

factors.note: Posts depend on KVS, NVS and other recruitments.

sources.title: Public notice: 22nd CTET on 12 and 13 December 2026 (14 Sep 2026)

gaps: Exact NCTE qualification combinations are summarised, not reproduced.
dataQuality.notes: Pattern, pass mark, validity, fee and dates from official CBSE documents.
